content.text:
I couldn't see the lines that send the mail, so this diagnosis is inferred from the retrieved snippets. The snippets show the profile email-change code signing a hash at `auth.service.ts` lines 492–505, but not the call that sends it. The sign-up mail is sent through `mailService.userSignUp`, which links to `confirm-email`. The e2e test expects the email-change mail to link to `confirm-new-email?hash=…`. That page is handled by `/auth/email/confirm/new`, which calls `confirmNewEmail`, the method that actually applies the new email.

I think the profile-update code sends the new-address mail with `mailService.userSignUp`, so it gets the sign-up link and never reaches `confirmNewEmail`. The alternative is that the mail service has no separate "new email" method, or has one that builds the wrong URL. I put that second.

candidates.explanation: After signing the email-change hash (which contains confirmEmailUserId and newEmail), the profile update sends the mail to the new address with the sign-up mail method (mailService.userSignUp). That method builds the sign-up activation link (confirm-email), not the confirm-new-email link. The hash is therefore consumed by the wrong page and /auth/email/confirm/new (confirmNewEmail) is never reached, so the email change is never applied. I could not see the actual send call, so this is inferred.

The mail service has no separate email-change mail method, or its URL is built with the sign-up path. The email-change mail must link to <frontend>/confirm-new-email?hash=..., as the e2e test expects. Because the method wasn't in the snippets, this is a fallback candidate.

fix.description: In the profile email-change branch, send the mail with a dedicated mailService.confirmNewEmail({to: userDto.email, data: {hash}}) instead of userSignUp. Make that mail method build the URL <frontendDomain>/confirm-new-email?hash=<hash> and use its own template and subject. The sign-up path stays on /confirm-email.
